I hit the tool limit mid-slice, so I don't have a finished archive for you. Rather than hand you a half-built tar, here's exactly where things stand and what I found — the reconnaissance is the valuable part, and the next session can pick it up cleanly.

First, a correction to my picture of the tree
My working memory said M6 Slice 4 with ten scenarios still skipped. The actual dump.txt is at M6 Slice 16 — all fifteen §16.3 scenarios are implemented (no [Fact(Skip)] placeholders left), and the backup/restore drill landed with F-38. BUILD_PROGRESS.md ends with "What is left in M6: Nothing. The next move is not a slice, it is a release."

So the next step is the release. Which is what I started building, and which turned up two gaps worth closing before the first tag rather than after.

What I verified
All the GitHub Action majors in your workflows exist. actions/checkout@v7, docker/setup-buildx-action@v4, docker/login-action@v4, docker/metadata-action@v6, docker/build-push-action@v7, actions/setup-dotnet@v6, actions/cache@v6, actions/upload-artifact@v7 — all real, all current. release.yml has never run; it would have.
Nothing in the tree stamps a version. Directory.Build.props sets no VersionPrefix, so every assembly reports the SDK's default 1.0.0, and Program.cs calls AddService(serviceName: "myrestaurant") with no serviceVersion. Every trace and metric leaving the box is unversioned, and a running instance cannot tell you what it is. That's fine while one person deploys by hand; it stops being fine the moment ghcr.io images exist for other people.
Relying on the SDK to append the commit doesn't work here. I read Microsoft.NET.GenerateAssemblyInfo.targets — AddSourceRevisionToInformationalVersion is gated on SourceControlInformationFeatureSupported, which SourceLink sets and nothing else in the SDK does. So SourceRevisionId alone is silently ignored. The fix is to pass InformationalVersion explicitly rather than take a package dependency for one string.
There is no AGPL §13 source offer. I read §13 out of your LICENSE: it binds whoever modifies the Program, so an unmodified deployment owes nothing — but CONTRIBUTING.md says "your fork owes its users the same," and nothing in the application makes that discharge-able. A fork operator currently complies by writing a page from scratch. Shipping the mechanism means they comply by setting one variable. Same shape as F-35/F-37: a thing the documents assume and no milestone claimed.
README.md is materially false. It claims eight of fifteen scenarios, M6 in progress, "the remaining seven scenarios and an executable backup/restore drill are what is left," and its Backups section describes the pre-Slice-16 script behaviour. It's the front door of a repo about to be tagged.
BUILD_PROGRESS.md's staged plan still has Stages 2–6 unchecked, with Stage 2 marked "in progress."
What I'd built before the limit
Staged at correct repo-relative paths, all full files:

Configuration/BuildInformation.cs — new; parses the informational version into version + revision, Current static, pure testable parse
Configuration/SourceRoutes.cs — new
Components/Pages/Source.razor — new; the offer, naming this build's revision
Components/Layout/AppColophon.razor — new; footer line, every page, both layouts
Configuration/RestaurantOptions.cs — RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL + validation (http and https accepted, deliberately, unlike the public origin)
Identity/ObligationsEnforcement.cs — /source exempted from the pipeline
MainLayout.razor, DisplayLayout.razor, wwwroot/app.css — colophon rendering and styling
Program.cs — one line: serviceVersion on the OTel resource
Directory.Build.props, Containerfile — the version/revision chain
.github/workflows/ci.yml — stamps the image, plus a new boot-smoke step that curls /source anonymously and fails unless the response contains github.sha
That last one is the piece I'd most want to keep: F-38's lesson was that a claim about behaviour should be checked by something that runs, and every link in the stamp chain fails silently — the page still renders, it just says "not recorded," which looks like a choice.

Still outstanding
release.yml (build-args from the tag, gh release create), the three tests, and all the documentation: REQUIREMENTS.md rev 3, spec v1.3 with a new §11.9 and F-39 in Appendix A, the ledger row, OPERATIONS.md, the BUILD_PROGRESS.md checkboxes and release section, the README rewrite, _CHANGES.md.

Say continue and I'll rebuild the staged files and finish it into one .tar.gz. Worth flagging: this slice is larger than a normal one because it's a release rather than a feature. If you'd rather split it — documentation-and-checkboxes now, the source offer and version stamp as their own slice after — say so and I'll cut it that way instead.

M6 close-out — the release. 26 full files, 5 of them new, extracting at the repo root. Files to DELETE: none.

bash
tar -xzf m6-closeout-release.tar.gz -C /home/kushal/src/dotnet/myrestaurant
_CHANGES.md has the full account. The short version of why there was a slice here at all:

Slice 16 said "the next move is not a slice, it is a release." True of the feature list, not of the tree. Reading the repo against what a tag would make true — rather than against §19 — turned up two things, and they're one thing:

Nothing could say which build it was. No VersionPrefix, so every assembly reported the SDK's default 1.0.0. AddService(serviceName: "myrestaurant") with no serviceVersion, so every trace left the process unversioned. The only answer to "which build is on that box" was whatever you typed when you deployed it.

Nothing offered anybody the source. AGPL §13 — read out of your own LICENSE, not recalled — asks a modified version to prominently offer users the corresponding source. R§1 says the project is published so anyone may run their own copy; CONTRIBUTING.md has told forks since rev 1 that "your fork owes its users the same." Nothing made that dischargeable. Same shape as F-35 and F-37: assumed by the documents, claimed by no milestone. It's F-39.

They land together because §13 offers the source of the version being interacted with — an offer that can't name a revision is approximate.

Three things I'd flag specifically:

The SourceLink trap. The obvious implementation is -p:SourceRevisionId=$SHA. It silently does nothing: AddSourceRevisionToInformationalVersion is gated on SourceControlInformationFeatureSupported, which a code search of dotnet/sdk finds in exactly two files — that target and its own test. SourceLink sets it; nothing else does. So the Containerfile passes InformationalVersion explicitly rather than taking a package dependency for one string.

The gate. F-38's lesson was that an embodiment row should name something executable, so boot-smoke now curls /source anonymously and fails unless the response contains github.sha. Every link in that stamp chain fails silently — the page still renders, it renders "Not recorded," which looks like a config choice. The commit appearing is the assertion nothing weaker satisfies.

Three stale claims fixed in passing. The spec header said v1.1 while its changelog carried v1.2. Every stage checkbox from 2 to 6 was unticked, Stage 2 still "in progress" through four completed milestones. And Home.razor told every visitor the event explorer "arrives next" — it shipped in M5.

Expected: dotnet build clean, dotnet test at 996 total / 0 failed / 982 succeeded / 14 skipped (+25 facts). Nothing compiled here — the verification list is in _CHANGES.md.

One decision to veto if you disagree: REQUIREMENTS.md moves to rev 3. That's the opposite call from Slice 16, and deliberately — §15's key-ring sentence was already the contract, so that was a mechanism-level fix. Here nothing previously said the program must name itself or offer its source. New intent, so the requirements move. Pulling it back out is one bullet and one history line.
